Let the number whose last two digits are crossed out be \(100q+r\), where \(0\le r\le 99\).  
The other number is \(5(q+1)=5q+5\).

Since their sum is \(2013\):
\[
100q+r+5q+5=2013
\]
\[
105q+r=2008
\]
With \(0\le r\le 99\), dividing gives:
\[
q=19,\quad r=13
\]
So the numbers are:
\[
100(19)+13=1913
\]
and
\[
5(19+1)=100
\]

The largest is \(\boxed{1913}\).
